spans.s:
raktá, ppl. colored; esp. red; as n. blood.
[√rañj, 954a.]

√1rakṣ (rákṣati, -te; rarákṣa; árakṣīt;
rakṣitá; rákṣitum; -rákṣya). de-fend,
protect; keep, i. e. both retain and maintain;
 take care of (as a sovereign), i. e.
govern; guard, ward; save. [a desid.
extension of √*rak or ark: cf. ἀλέξ-ω,
‘ward off,’ which bears a similar relation
to √ἀλκ or ἀρκ in ἄλ-αλκ-ε, ‘warded off,’
ἀρκ-έω, ‘ward off, protect’; cf. also Lat.
arc-eo, ‘ward off,’ arx, ‘stronghold of defence,
 citadel’; AS. ealh-stede, ‘defencestead,
 strong-hold’; ealgian, ‘protect’:
for the two chief mgs of √rakṣ, cf. Lat.
de-fendere, ‘ward off, protect.’]
+ pari, protect around; save.

√2rakṣ, harm, in rakṣas. [perhaps only
another aspeet of 1rakṣ, ‘ward off,’ i. e.
‘beat away.’]

rákṣas, n.
 —1. harm;
 —2. concrete,
harmer, name of nocturnal demons who
disturb sacrifices and harm the pious.
[√2rakṣ, 1151. 2a.]

rakṣi, a. guarding, at end of cpds.
[√1rakṣ, 1155.]

rākṣasa, a. demoniacal; as m. a demoniacal
one, a Rakshas. [rákṣas, q. v.,
1208a.]
